note: Bytes in and bytes out (CyberChef's Input and Output menus are chain steps such as hex:decode and hex:encode). Key and IV are key params in any key encoding; the key is 8 bytes. Modes CBC (default), CFB, OFB, CTR and ECB as in CyberChef, with the shared blockmode layer; padding is its own choice (pkcs7 or none). A wrong key or IV length is E_RANGE. CTR adds one to the last four bytes of the counter block only, modulo 2^32 with no carry into the rest, as CyberChef does (node-forge's inc32); a whole-block counter (the usual reading of SP 800-38A) gives the same key stream until the low word wraps, after 2^32 blocks.
The inverse of des:encrypt with the same parameters; bad PKCS#7 padding or ciphertext that is not whole 8-byte blocks is E_COERCE.

As DES with a 24-byte key, or a 16-byte key (two-key: K3 = K1, as CyberChef does); modes CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR and ECB; padding is its own choice. EDE form (SP 800-67). CTR adds one to the last four bytes of the counter block only, modulo 2^32 with no carry into the rest, as CyberChef does (node-forge's inc32); a whole-block counter (the usual reading of SP 800-38A) gives the same key stream until the low word wraps, after 2^32 blocks.
The inverse of triple-des:encrypt with the same parameters.

Key of 4 to 56 bytes (CyberChef's range), modes CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR and ECB, padding as a separate choice (pkcs7 or none). Big-endian words as in Schneier's paper. CTR adds one to the last four bytes of the counter block only, modulo 2^32 with no carry into the rest, as CyberChef does (node-forge's inc32); a whole-block counter (the usual reading of SP 800-38A) gives the same key stream until the low word wraps, after 2^32 blocks.
The inverse of blowfish:encrypt with the same parameters.

RFC 2268. CyberChef runs CBC when an IV is given and ECB when it is blank, with no other setting; here mode (CBC, the default, or ECB) is explicit, so a blank IV in CBC is E_RANGE. The RFC's effective key bits are the effective-bits param (1 to 1024), whose default 128 is what CyberChef's library uses for any key length. Key 1 to 128 bytes; padding is its own choice. Effective bits that are not a multiple of 8 follow RFC 2268 (the vectors cover 63 and 129); the library behind CyberChef masks those wrongly, but CyberChef never sets them.
The inverse of rc2:encrypt with the same parameters, including effective-bits.

RC6-w/r with CyberChef's parameters: word-size (a multiple of 8, 8 to 256, default 32) and rounds (1 to 255, default 20); an empty IV is zero bytes as in CyberChef; modes CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR and ECB. Padding is pkcs7 or none: CyberChef's ZERO, RANDOM and BIT paddings are not offered (the shared padding is PKCS#7), and empty input encrypts to one padding block where CyberChef returns nothing. Word sizes other than 32 use BigInt arithmetic and are slow. CTR reads the counter block as a little-endian integer (the first byte is the least significant) and adds one per block, as CyberChef's RC6 does, so it differs from the big-endian counter of the other ciphers after the first block. The block is w / 2 bytes, so word-size 8 has 4-byte blocks (the modes work for any block size).
The inverse of rc6:encrypt with the same parameters.

Keys of 16, 24 or 32 bytes, 16-byte IV, modes CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR and ECB. Padding is pkcs7 or none: CyberChef's ZERO, RANDOM and BIT paddings are not offered. CTR reads the counter block as a little-endian integer (the first byte is the least significant) and adds one per block, as CyberChef's Twofish does, so it differs from the big-endian counter of the other ciphers after the first block. An empty input encrypts to one block of padding in CBC and ECB where CyberChef returns nothing.
The inverse of twofish:encrypt with the same parameters.

GB/T 32907-2016, 16-byte key and IV, modes CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR and ECB. CyberChef's CBC/NoPadding and ECB/NoPadding modes are padding none. CTR adds one to the last four bytes of the counter block only, modulo 2^32 with no carry into the rest, as CyberChef does (node-forge's inc32); a whole-block counter (the usual reading of SP 800-38A) gives the same key stream until the low word wraps, after 2^32 blocks. An empty input encrypts to one block of padding in CBC and ECB where CyberChef returns nothing.
The inverse of sm4:encrypt with the same parameters.
